From b08abbd9f5996309f021684f9ca74da30dcca36a Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Quinn Tran <quinn.tran@cavium.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Jul 2018 14:29:54 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] scsi: qla2xxx: Fix ISP recovery on unload

During unload process, the chip can encounter problem where a FW dump would
be captured. For this case, the full reset sequence will be skip to bring
the chip back to full operational state.

Fixes: e315cd28b9ef ("[SCSI] qla2xxx: Code changes for qla data structure refactoring")
Cc: <stable@vger.kernel.org>
Signed-off-by: Quinn Tran <quinn.tran@cavium.com>
Signed-off-by: Himanshu Madhani <himanshu.madhani@cavium.com>
Signed-off-by: Martin K. Petersen <martin.petersen@oracle.com>

diff --git a/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_os.c b/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_os.c
index 2cd2e5ccce15..1fbd16c8c9a7 100644
--- a/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_os.c
+++ b/drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_os.c
@@ -6020,8 +6020,9 @@ qla2x00_do_dpc(void *data)
 				set_bit(ISP_ABORT_NEEDED, &base_vha->dpc_flags);
 		}
 
-		if (test_and_clear_bit(ISP_ABORT_NEEDED,
-						&base_vha->dpc_flags)) {
+		if (test_and_clear_bit
+		    (ISP_ABORT_NEEDED, &base_vha->dpc_flags) &&
+		    !test_bit(UNLOADING, &base_vha->dpc_flags)) {
 
 			ql_dbg(ql_dbg_dpc, base_vha, 0x4007,
 			    "ISP abort scheduled.\n");
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/scsi/qla2xxx/qla_os.c`**
   - A conditional check was modified in the `qla2x00_do_dpc` function.
   - The original condition that checked if `ISP_ABORT_NEEDED` was set has been updated to also check that the `UNLOADING` flag is not set. This means that the ISP abort will only be scheduled if the system is not in the process of unloading.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `qla_os.c` addresses a specific issue during the unload process of the SCSI driver for the qla2xxx series. By adding the check for the `UNLOADING` flag, the patch ensures that the full reset sequence is skipped when a firmware dump is captured during the unload, thereby preventing potential issues that could arise from attempting to abort operations while unloading. This change is directly related to the bug fix described in the patch, which aims to improve the recovery process of the ISP during the unload phase.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
if (test_and_clear_bit(ISP_ABORT_NEEDED, &base_vha->dpc_flags)) {
```
```c
if (qlafx00_reset_initialize(base_vha)) {
```
```c
set_bit(ISP_UNRECOVERABLE, &base_vha->dpc_flags);
```
Reason:
During the unload process, the code attempts to perform an ISP abort without checking if the system is in the process of unloading. This can lead to an incomplete or erroneous state of the chip, as the abort operation may not be appropriate when the driver is unloading, potentially causing the chip to fail to recover properly.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (test_and_clear_bit(ISP_ABORT_NEEDED, &base_vha->dpc_flags) &&
    !test_bit(UNLOADING, &base_vha->dpc_flags)) {
```
```c
set_bit(ISP_UNRECOVERABLE, &base_vha->dpc_flags);
```
Reason:
The fix adds a condition to check if the system is unloading before proceeding with the ISP abort. This ensures that the abort operation is only executed when the system is not in the process of unloading, thus preventing the chip from entering an erroneous state and allowing it to recover properly.
